title: Suppliers Cybersecurity Maturity Self-Attestation and Evidence Checklist (template)
body:
Purpose:

This is a supplier-facing self-attestation template intended to provide a concise, pragmatic way for prospective and existing vendors to document their cybersecurity maturity across control areas most relevant to Redwood Inference. The form is designed for rapid intake (estimate: 45–90 minutes dependent on evidence availability) and to produce a consistent artifact that can be reviewed by our Third-Party Risk team.

How to use this template:

- Supplier completes sections 1–6 and attaches evidence files or links where indicated.
- Supplier provides one short narrative per control (max 150 words) describing how the control is implemented in practice and where evidence can be found.
- Supplier self-rates maturity using the 0–4 scale below and selects applicable evidence items from the checklist.
- Third-Party Risk reviewer will validate critical controls and may request follow-up evidence or a short remediation plan.

Maturity scale (self-rating):
0 — Not applicable / no capability
1 — Ad hoc / documented only
2 — Basic repeatable process in place
3 — Formalized process with measurable metrics
4 — Optimized and continuously improved (benchmarking, automation)

1) Company & engagement metadata:
- Legal entity name (as on contract):
- Primary contact: name, role, email, phone:
- Scope of services provided to Redwood (short):
- Data classes processed (select): PII, customer content, logs/telemetry, model inputs, health metrics, other (specify)
- Deployment model delivered to Redwood: Hosted API | Dedicated | Private (VPC/on-prem)

2) High-level attestation summary (one paragraph):
- Provide a 2–3 sentence summary of overall security posture, recent audits/certifications (ISO27001, SOC2 Type II, PCI, etc.), and ownership of security incidents over the last 24 months (Y/N — provide short context).

3) Control areas, self-rating, evidence checklist, and narrative (repeat per area):
(Organize submissions by control area. Supplier must provide at least one evidence item per control rated >=2.)

A. Data protection and encryption (key controls: encryption at rest, encryption in transit, key management, separation of customer keys):
- Self-rating (0–4):
- Narrative (max 150 words):
- Evidence checklist (pick all that apply):
  - Encryption algorithm and key length documentation (e.g., TLS config, AES specs)
  - KMS/HSM architecture diagram and key rotation policy
  - Process for customer-supplied keys (BYOK) or proof of segregation of keys per customer
  - Sample configuration file or network policy showing TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 enforcement
  - Logs or screenshots showing encryption metrics or key rotation events

B. Access control and identity management (IAM, RBAC, SSO, privileged access):
- Self-rating (0–4):
- Narrative (max 150 words):
- Evidence checklist (pick all that apply):
  - IAM role definitions and RBAC matrix for service accounts and human users
  - SSO/SAML/OIDC configuration and IdP vendor name
  - Privileged access review policy and recent review report (<90 days)
  - MFA enforcement evidence for admin and developer accounts

C. Secure software development and supply chain controls (SDLC, code signing, CI/CD hardening):
- Self-rating (0–4):
- Narrative (max 150 words):
- Evidence checklist (pick all that apply):
  - Secure coding standards and code review policy
  - CI/CD pipeline diagram showing build/test/signing steps
  - Example of signed artifact metadata or code-signing key custody description
  - SCA (software composition analysis) results summary for a recent build

D. Infrastructure and runtime security (network segmentation, container/orchestration hardening, host patching):
- Self-rating (0–4):
- Narrative (max 150 words):
- Evidence checklist (pick all that apply):
  - Network diagram showing segmentation and control plane isolation
  - Host/OS patch policy and recent patch compliance report
  - Container image vulnerability scan report for a production image
  - Runtime hardening checklist (AppArmor/SELinux, seccomp profiles)

E. Logging, monitoring, and incident response (detection, alerting, IR playbooks, SLAs):
- Self-rating (0–4):
- Narrative (max 150 words):
- Evidence checklist (pick all that apply):
  - SIEM coverage diagram and key alerting rules for high-risk events
  - Recent tabletop or incident response exercise summary (within 12 months)
  - Incident response playbook excerpt showing escalation and customer notification timelines
  - Pager/on-call rotation documentation and mean time to detect/mean time to respond metrics if available

F. Data lifecycle and deletion (retention, deletion on contract termination, backups):
- Self-rating (0–4):
- Narrative (max 150 words):
- Evidence checklist (pick all that apply):
  - Data retention schedule and justification per data class
  - Procedure and checklist for data deletion upon contract termination
  - Backup architecture and restoration/test logs showing success of restores
  - Example deletion confirmation artifact that could be shared with Redwood under NDA

G. Privacy & data processing (subprocessors, DPIA, cross-border transfers):
- Self-rating (0–4):
- Narrative (max 150 words):
- Evidence checklist (pick all that apply):
  - Current subprocessors list with locations and data classes processed
  - Data protection impact assessment (DPIA) or privacy risk assessment summary for the services in scope
  - Standard contractual clauses or other transfer mechanism documentation, if applicable

4) Third-party validation and certifications:
- List any independent attestations relevant to security and privacy (SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, PCI DSS, etc.) and provide date and scope of most recent assessment. Attach or link to the attestation report or an auditor contact.

5) Known issues, recent incidents, and corrective actions (last 24 months):
- Briefly describe any security incidents that impacted customer data or operations; include high-level root cause and remediation measures. If none, state "No incidents impacting customer data or production services in last 24 months."

6) Remediation roadmap (if any control is rated 0–2):
- For each control rated 0–2, provide: planned remediation action, target completion date, owner (name + role), and any blockers.

7) Scoring rubric and threshold guidance (internal use):
- Suggested internal interpretation (do not include in supplier submission unless requested):
  - Green (acceptable): Average >= 3 and no critical control rated 0–1
  - Yellow (requires conditional acceptance / remediation plan): Average between 2.0 and 2.9 or any critical control rated 2 with remediation <90 days
  - Red (not acceptable): Any critical control rated 0–1, or average <2.0
- Critical controls (examples): encryption at rest, network TLS for customer traffic, admin MFA, incident notification within contract SLA window

8) Evidence packaging checklist (for supplier):
- Prefer single ZIP with filename pattern vendorname-YYYYMMDD-evidence.zip or secure links (Do not include secrets or private keys)
- Include a short index.csv describing each file, its corresponding control, and page/section references for long documents
- If evidence includes screenshots, include timestamps and brief captions explaining what is shown

9) Sign-off and attestation language (sample):
- "I confirm that the information provided in this self-attestation and the attached evidence is accurate to the best of my knowledge and that I am authorized to provide this information on behalf of [Legal Entity]. I understand that Redwood Inference may verify information provided and request additional evidence.

  Name:
  Title:
  Date:
  Contact email:"

10) Internal reviewer notes (placeholder for Redwood use):
- Risk owner:
- Preliminary score:
- Review date:
- Follow-up items and owner:

Appendix A — Example evidence artifacts (non-exhaustive):
- Redacted SOC 2 encryption control narrative, KMS configuration snippet, IdP metadata export, recent pentest executive summary, sample RBAC matrix, pipeline signing metadata, restoration test logs.

Appendix B — Quick triage flow (internal):
- If supplier scores Red on any critical control -> escalate to Security Director and pause onboarding until mitigation plan accepted.
- If Yellow -> require remedial plan and milestone checks before production access.
- If Green -> proceed with contract and schedule periodic revalidation (annual for high-risk services).

Notes and versioning:
- Template owner: Security & Compliance (evan.brooks@redwood.ai)
- Template version: 0.2-draft
- Intended audience: procurement, solutions engineering, vendor security, third-party risk reviewers

(End of template)
